body:
Small fixes and additions to the stable C++ API (`tools/cpp`), found while porting [duckdb-odbc](https://github.com/Robinho-MR/duckdb-odbc/pull/1) from DuckDB's internal C++ classes to `duckdb::cxx`. None of them changes the C API or the engine.

### `StartupOptions::Set(name, value)`

`StartupOptions` only had five dedicated setters, while `duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options` accepts any option by name. So the C++ API couldn't set any startup-only option that lacks a setter, for example:
- `duckdb_api`, which every client sets to identify itself (the ODBC driver sets `odbc`);
- `access_mode`;
- `extension_repository_directory`;
- any startup-only option a user puts in a connection string.

`Set` forwards a (name, value) pair to the C API, in the textual form SQL `SET` accepts. Pairs are applied in the order given, after the dedicated setters, so a later value wins. Options that need a running instance (`allowed_directories`, ...) still go through `Instance::GetConfig()`, as the C API documents.

### `Value::GetDecimal()` and a public `Value::CreateDecimal()`

`Value::Get<WIDTH, SCALE>()` and `Value::Create(decimal_t<WIDTH, SCALE>)` need the width and scale at compile time. A driver learns them at runtime, from a result column (`SQL_C_NUMERIC`) or a bound parameter (`SQL_NUMERIC` with a precision and scale). Until now it couldn't read the unscaled integer of a DECIMAL, nor create one, without going through text.

- `Value::GetDecimal()` returns a `RuntimeDecimal {int128_t value; uint8_t width; uint8_t scale;}`, through `duckdb_v2_value_get_decimal`.
- `Value::CreateDecimal(factory, int128_t value, width, scale)` was already the private runtime forwarder of the typed constructor; it is now public and documented.
- C API change: `duckdb_v2_value_create_decimal` now returns `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` for a value with more digits than the declared width. Before, it only checked the storage tier, so e.g. 10000 at `DECIMAL(4,0)` (or anything past 10^38 at width 38) built a value that failed on bind or asserted in `ToText()`. INT16 and INT32 tier overflows used to surface as an INTERNAL cast error; they are now `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` too.

### Compile when `<windows.h>` was included first

`<windows.h>` defines `DELETE` and `IGNORE` as macros. That turns the `StatementType::DELETE` and `FunctionCollationHandling::IGNORE` enumerators into syntax errors for any Windows consumer that includes it before `duckdb_cpp.hpp`, which an ODBC driver must. The header now sets both macros aside with `push_macro`/`pop_macro` while it is parsed. These two are the only Windows macros among the header's enumerators. Separately, `AddString` and `AddBlob` now call `(std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)()`, so the `max` macro (without `NOMINMAX`) does not break them.

### Tests

New cases in `tools/cpp/tests` cover:
- startup-only options and aliases, override order, bad values and unknown names;
- options that need a running instance;
- runtime DECIMALs across every storage tier, the typed constructor, a query result, and out-of-range width, scale and value, plus non-DECIMAL and NULL values.

`unittest "[cpp_api]"`: all 218 test cases pass (4248 assertions).

comments.body: Merged main in e08a632a0f7 to resolve the conflict with #26955 (DECIMAL widths up to 255). The width check from 1f8d0a3c2ad now applies only to widths below 39: a 128-bit value always fits a wider decimal, which is stored as BIGNUM. The `value_create_decimal` docs combine the 1..255 range with the digit check. I also dropped the C++ API test expecting width 39 to be rejected, since main now accepts it. `[cpp_api]` and `[capi_v2]` pass on reldebug.

review_comments.body:
`<windows.h>` compatibility remains incomplete at `tools/cpp/duckdb_cpp.hpp:51`. Without `NOMINMAX`, its `max(a, b)` macro breaks `AddString` and `AddBlob` at `tools/cpp/duckdb_cpp.hpp:2453` and `tools/cpp/duckdb_cpp.hpp:2468`: `macro "max" requires 2 arguments, but only 1 given`. This is pre-existing and outside the enumerators, so the description's enumerator claim holds. libstdc++ hides it by undefining macros present before standard headers; gcc and clang fail when macros follow those headers, as with MSVC's STL. Parenthesizing both calls fixes those builds; MSVC was unavailable:

```cpp
		if (data.size() > (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)()) {
```

The assertion at `tools/cpp/tests/test_cpp_api_types_values.cpp:504` also passes before this PR. `Exception` catches both the old `INTERNAL Error: Information loss on integer cast` and the new invalid input error for INT16/INT32 overflow (`40000` at width 4, `3000000000` at width 9). Consequently, it does not pin the improvement. I would check `HasErrorCode(DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_INVALID)` here, add the INT32 case below, and note the v2 C API behavior change in the description, which currently says there is none. These test and description changes need not block.

```cpp
	REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(Value::CreateDecimal(factory, int128_t {3000000000ULL, 0}, 9, 0), Exception,
	                       HasErrorCode(DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_INVALID));
```

Fixed in 1f8d0a3c2ad. `BuildDecimal` now checks `|value| < 10^width` after validating width and scale, then picks the hugeint or int64 form, using the check you suggested. `TRY`-less creation of `10000` at `DECIMAL(4,0)` or `{0, INT64_MIN}` at width 38 now returns `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. The `duckdb_v2.h` / `value.yaml` docs now say so instead of "not range-checked against the width".
Fixed in 1f8d0a3c2ad: both calls in `AddString` and `AddBlob` are now `(std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)()`. I have not built with MSVC either.

Done in 1f8d0a3c2ad. The tests now check `HasErrorCode(DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_INVALID)` for 10000 and 40000 at width 4, 3000000000 at width 9, `{0, INT64_MIN}` and 10^38 at width 38, and that 9999 at width 4 and 10^38 - 1 at width 38 are accepted. The description now lists the v2 C API behavior change. `[cpp_api]` (218 cases) and `[capi_v2]` (597 cases) pass on reldebug.

Verified the fix in `1f8d0a3c2ad`: `CreateDecimal` rejects 10000 and -10000 at width 4, 10^9 at width 9, 10^18 at width 18, 2^100 at width 30, and both `INT128` limits at width 38 with an invalid input error. It accepts 9999, -9999 and the PR's own cases; width 39 and above is accepted using the wide decimal support from main.
